paper: C. R. Menyuk, Nonlinear pulse propagation in birefringent optical fibers, IEEE J. Quantum Electron. QE-23, 174 (1987)
description: Normalized vector NLSE (8a/8b) with the 2/3 XPM factor and oscillating FWM term: (i) scalar single-polarization soliton Eq. (9), (ii) exact two-polarization locked vector soliton Eq. (10) — each axis carries 3/5 of the scalar peak — as a filament-identity check, (iii) the locking -> linear-splitting bifurcation over 20 km located at delta* ~ 0.04.
note_scalars: Same physical fiber profile as the Manakov reproduction (n2 = 2.6e-20 m2/W, A_eff = 52 um2 at 1550 nm gives gamma = 2.027e-3 W-1 m-1). The paper works in normalized units; the physical anchors z0 (0.71 km, 1.8 m) fix beta2 exactly via beta2 = -pi t0^2/(2 z0). The printed D(lambda) = 6.5e-3 s/m has ambiguous digitized units and is not used numerically; z0 is the paper's stated value. Cross-check: D(1.55 um) ~ 14 ps/(nm km) for the derived beta2, a standard 1987 dispersion-shifted telecom fiber.

conventions.z0: z0 = pi^2 c tau0^2 / (D(lambda) lambda0); xi = pi z / (2 z0)
conventions.t0: T0 = tau / 1.763 (tau = intensity FWHM; 0.568 tau = (1/1.763) tau sech convention)
conventions.beta2: beta2 = -pi t0^2 / (2 z0) (anomalous, sech solitons); anchored by the paper's z0 values
conventions.delta: delta = (k1 - l1) t0 / (2|beta2|); group-delay mismatch in |beta2| units
conventions.walkoff_engine: Delta_beta1 = 2 |beta2| delta / t0 = pi delta t0 / z0 (SI s/m; engine walkoff = beta1_y - beta1_x, paper's 2 delta drift between the axes in the mean frame)
conventions.delta_beta_engine: FWM mismatch: paper phase R delta xi = R delta pi z / (2 z0) enters the engine as e^{+-2i Delta_beta z} with Delta_beta = R delta pi / (4 z0)
conventions.scalar_soliton_peak: P1 = |beta2| / (gamma t0^2); vector-soliton per-axis peak P_axis = (3/5) P1 (each axis carries 3/5 of the scalar intensity, total 6/5)
conventions.chirps_eq10: launch u = v = sqrt(3/5 P1) sech(t/t0) exp(-+ i delta t/t0) with engine walkoff = Delta_beta1: the +- chirps each contribute +- half the walk-off, so the coincident lock stays coincident in the engine x-retarded frame

scan.split_criterion: x-y intensity overlap < 0.5 vs linear (gamma=0) reference run with the same walkoff

case_250fs.note: R delta <= 1 for delta <= 1.4e-3: only regime where the FWM term must be kept; delta = 0.1 gives R delta = 70 (FWM beat length ~20 cm, resolvable).
